# Efficiency & Deployment

[← Catalog](../../README.md) · [All topics](../README.md) · [Search website](https://byby221b.github.io/Awesome-CTR-Scaling/?category=efficiency-deployment)

Training, inference and deployment techniques that make model scaling practical.

| <a id="paper-2602-10455"></a>**UG-Sep: Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models** | ByteDance | arXiv | 2026 | `Serving` `Training Efficiency` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10455) | UG-Sep makes user-side computation reusable inside TokenMixer-style feature-interaction models. It separates user-only token flows from item-conditioned flows, then compensates for interactions suppressed by that separation. Weight-only quantization addresses the memory bottleneck exposed after redundant compute is removed, linking architectural reuse with hardware-level efficiency. |
| <a id="paper-2607-28940"></a>**TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings** | LinkedIn | KDD (ADS) | 2026 | `Serving` `Attention` `Long Sequence` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28940) | TransX separates long-term behavior streams from real-time serving events instead of flattening both into one sequence. Nearline behavior encodings condition an online action decoder through cross-attention. Incremental updates and per-request caching amortize history processing, keeping request-time work less dependent on the full behavior-sequence length. |
| <a id="paper-2607-12281"></a>**SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart** | Meta | arXiv | 2026 | `Serving` `Long Sequence` `User Modeling` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12281) | SlimPer represents ranking as repeated refinement of a compact user–item state. Each layer queries raw multimodal user tokens, computes relevance matches and updates that fixed-size state, rather than carrying a large sequence-shaped hidden tensor through every layer. Shared user tokens across candidates further reduce memory duplication while retaining access to detailed histories. |
| <a id="paper-2605-24989"></a>**Selective Test-Time Compute Scaling for CTR Prediction via Uncertainty-Triggered Feature Path Exploration** | Alibaba | arXiv | 2026 | `Test-time Compute` `Sparse Activation` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24989) | UTTSI allocates extra inference work to uncertain examples without retraining the underlying click model. Confidence and feature-frequency signals guide filtering; uncertain inputs then receive stochastic feature-path exploration, whose predictions are combined by consistency. The method tests selective prediction ensembling rather than spending the same extra compute on every request. |
| <a id="paper-2512-07650"></a>**Exploring Test-time Scaling via Prediction Merging on Large-Scale Recommendation** | Academic | SIGIR | 2026 | `Test-time Compute` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.07650) | This study scales recommendation inference by merging predictions from diverse models, using either different architectures or different initializations of the same architecture. It compares that use of compute with enlarging a single model under matched inference budgets. Parallel serving can limit user-visible latency, but the benefit still requires additional aggregate inference resources. |
| <a id="paper-2609-02671"></a>**DS-Frame: Recommender System as Slow and Fast Thinkers** | Academic | arXiv | 2026 | `Test-time Compute` `Sequence Modeling` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02671) | DS-Frame gives a sequential recommender a fast path for routine predictions and a slower path that iteratively refines latent representations. A learned selector decides which samples receive extra work under a controllable compute budget. The experiments focus on whether harder groups, such as users with long or less-mainstream histories, benefit from this adaptive allocation. |
| <a id="paper-2609-01807"></a>**SPD: Single Pass Decoding for Generative Reranking** | Amazon | arXiv | 2026 | `Test-time Compute` `Generative Rec` `Serving` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01807) | SPD exploits the fact that reranking outputs a permutation of known items rather than arbitrary text. A lightweight head reads item–position scores from the language model's prefill states, and an assignment algorithm produces a valid order in a constant number of model passes. This replaces sequential token decoding, though score construction and assignment still depend on the candidate set. |
